Issued at 203 PM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Rest of Today-Tonight...High pressure over the northern Gulf Coast 
maintains northeasterly flow across the forecast area today. PWATs 
below 1.5" and strong subsidence in the mid-levels has, so far, 
prevented most shower development through early this afternoon. 
However, a scattered stratocu deck has developed across east central 
Florida and a shower or two has been observed on KMLB radar 
northeast of Cape Canaveral over the Atlantic waters. Expect similar 
conditions to persist into tonight. But, while subsidence aloft 
continues into Wednesday, the plume of moisture around 900mb that is 
currently generating our afternoon cloud deck will support a few 
showers over the Atlantic waters overnight. So, have maintained 15-
20% PoPs along the coast, especially after midnight, as a few of 
those showers drift onshore. NE winds around 10-12 mph this 
afternoon will become light after sunset, though may remain around 
10 mph along the barrier islands. Temperatures look to fall into the 
upper 60s to lower 70s west of I-95 late tonight, but onshore flow 
will keep coastal areas in the mid-70s.

Wednesday-Thursday...A trough digging through the Great Lakes mid-
week will shift the ridge over the Southeast US offshore through 
Thursday. Winds become increasingly easterly as the high shifts, 
becoming 10-15 mph each afternoon. As the wind direction changes, 
additional moisture will advect into the area building PWATs to 1.7-
2" by Thursday afternoon. A low chance for showers (15-20%) returns 
to most of the area Wednesday, though the greatest chance will be 
along the coast, especially south of Melbourne. Rain chances then 
build Thursday, becoming 30-50% south of Orlando Thursday afternoon. 
Rounds of showers will remain possible along the coast overnight, 
especially along the Treasure Coast. Thunder chances remain low, 
though a few storms will be possible Thursday afternoon as 
subsidence aloft wanes CAPE increases. High temperatures climb into 
the upper 80s to near 90, with overnight lows in the lower to mid-
70s.

Friday-Monday (modified previous)...High pressure ridge and onshore 
flow weakens Friday, as a cold front sweeps through the southeast 
U.S. and eventually across the area into Saturday. Winds briefly 
become northerly as front moves through, but strong area of high 
pressure that builds in well north of the front will quickly turn 
winds onshore into the weekend. A tightening pressure gradient 
between the front and ridge to the north will lead to breezy to 
windy conditions developing behind this boundary as early as 
Saturday and likely persisting through early next week. Rain chances 
remain near to above normal through the period, with scattered to 
numerous showers and isolated to scattered storms each day. This 
activity will mostly be limited to the afternoon and early evening 
hours on Friday. However, into the weekend and through Monday, deep 
moisture combined with strong low level onshore flow will continue 
rounds of gusty showers and storms pushing onshore. Locally heavy to 
excessive rainfall could also be possible, mainly along the coast 
where any persistent bands of showers and storms can develop. 
Coastal areas have already been highlighted in a Marginal Risk (1/4) 
for excessive rainfall on Saturday. 

The longer duration windy east-northeast flow into early next week 
will also lead to the development of dangerous surf and boating 
conditions, increasing the potential for beach erosion this weekend 
into early next week. Max temps will still reach the mid to upper 
80s on Friday, but are forecast to trend slightly cooler behind the 
front, falling to the low to mid 80s most days Saturday through 
Tuesday, though upper 70s to low 80s are forecast on Sunday. 
Overnight lows will remain near to above normal as gusty onshore 
flow continues.
